name: MQTT Notifications
author: ChuckBuilds
description: Display text or images from HomeAssistant via MQTT. Supports dynamic MQTT topics with wildcard support for flexible notification handling that interrupts the normal display rotation.

versions.changelog: Scrolling text moves smoothly: the plugin asks the core for its fast display loop while scrolling is on (it ran once a second, so text jumped 30px at a time), and it resumes where it left off instead of jumping after the screen has been away.

Saved settings now apply without a restart. The core applies a web-UI save by calling on_config_change, not by reloading the plugin, and the base version only replaces self.config, so the broker, topics, font and colours kept their old values. The connection is stopped, __init__ reads every setting again, and it reconnects; a notification already on screen stays.

Hides display_duration (each message sets its own screen time, else display.default_duration) and update_interval (update() does nothing; messages arrive on the MQTT thread). No behaviour change: hidden keys stay declared, so saved configs still load.

The MQTT connection is supervised the way pomodoro-timer does it, so one client exists at a time. The loop checked for a connection straight after loop_start(), before the broker could answer, so it kept building new clients without stopping the old ones; each kept reconnecting under the same client id, and the broker dropped one to admit another. A refused login retried with no delay. The loop now waits up to 5 s for the broker's answer, tears a failed client down before redialling, and backs off 1, 2, 4 ... 60 s. on_disable and cleanup release the client even if the loop thread has died.

Notifications now interrupt the rotation, as the README describes. The message was stored with cache_manager.set(..., max_age=3600), but the core's set() takes ttl, so the call raised TypeError, the handler logged it, and the on-demand request that follows it was never written: a notification waited for the plugin's turn in rotation instead. The call now passes ttl.
Render text 1-bit (no anti-aliasing) so glyphs stay crisp on the LED grid

versions.notes: Load a bitmap font at its own pixel size, and drop one that has no font file. A .bdf exists at exactly one pixel size and FreeType rejects any other, so every .bdf in the font picker failed at the configured font_size and silently fell back to the default face -- choosing one appeared to do nothing. Bitmap faces are now retried at the size the file's PIXEL_SIZE header declares. cozette.bdf is removed from the picker: the file is shipped by neither the core nor the plugin, so it could only ever fall back. Same fix already landed for clock-simple, news and tide-display, which share this loader.
changes: Documented the five remaining settings and added rendered examples of the scroll toggle, the appearance options, and four panel sizes.
